items.title: How many choices are covered?
body: Eight base classes and the 22 ascendancies available in the current 0.5 reference set.

items.title: What should decide the class?
body: The intended skill family, defensive model, resource engine and tolerance for setup—not a tier-list position alone.

items.title: Can another class use the same skill?
body: Usually yes. Starting location and ascendancy change efficiency and mechanics, while skill requirements and weapon rules still apply.

items.title: When should I reroll?
body: Reroll when the desired mechanic belongs to a different ascendancy; fix gear and skill links first when the problem is only damage or survival.

sections.title: How to use this guide
paragraphs: A base class determines the starting point and campaign identity; an ascendancy supplies specialised rules that can change how charges, gems, companions, defenses, or skills work. Choose the mechanic you want to play, then select the class that reaches it with the fewest forced compromises.

The summaries below describe tendencies rather than locking skills to classes. Patch notes can move individual nodes, so confirm the current ascendancy panel before following an older planner screenshot.

sections.title: Practical workflow
sections.intro: Run the process in order and preserve a rollback point before spending heavily.

cards.title: Step 1
body: Choose one primary skill or mechanic and list its weapon, tags, resource cost and required combat range.

cards.title: Step 2
body: Choose a defensive model that can function at that range: armour, evasion, Energy Shield, block, recovery, or a deliberate combination.

cards.title: Step 3
body: Shortlist ascendancies whose defining nodes improve both the mechanic and the real rotation.

cards.title: Step 4
body: Check the passive-tree distance, attributes and campaign levelling path before committing.

cards.title: Step 5
body: Use an early-map checkpoint: if the problem is gear, fix gear; if the desired mechanic is missing, reroll before further investment.

items.question: Can I change ascendancy?
answer: Follow the current in-game respec rules and cost; do not assume a guide from another patch still describes the process.

items.question: Which class is best for a beginner?
answer: A class whose core loop is understandable and whose defenses work on rare gear—often Titan, Deadeye or a straightforward caster, depending on preferred combat.

items.question: Are all ascendancies equally complete?
answer: Early Access balance and content evolve. Evaluate the nodes available in the current client, not launch-era expectations.

items.question: Should I start from the class or the skill?
answer: Start from the skill and playstyle, then choose the ascendancy that supplies the most valuable mechanical rule.

items.question: When is an off-class skill worth it?
answer: When the ascendancy interaction outweighs extra passive travel, attributes and gear pressure.
